idiom_name: static factory method on the aggregate (Order.open) + private constructor; standalone injected factory class for cross-aggregate creation
implementation_notes: A Java constructor cannot return a failure value, so the idiomatic factory is a static method with a domain name (Order.open, Subscription.startNew) that validates, computes and then calls a private constructor; records with compact constructors cover value-shaped products and Optional.of/ofNullable covers nullable single values without inventing exception types. What replaces the classic factory class is the static factory method on the aggregate itself; keep a separate, constructor-injected factory class behind an interface only when creation must load other aggregates or consult a domain service, and remember that persistence frameworks need a non-private constructor.
pitfalls: JPA/Hibernate and Jackson need a no-arg or protected constructor; keep it non-public, annotate it as infrastructure-only and never rely on it to enforce invariants.
Static factories are hard for IDEs and readers to discover because they are not constructors; document every creation path in the class comment or migrate to a factory type when the list grows.
Overloads whose parameter lists differ only in order or type are indistinguishable at the call site; one domain name per creation path instead of many constructors.
